primitives.name: Retinal Quadrant Mapping
primitives.verbatim_quote: This theory starts from the truth that on both retins an impression on the upper half makes us perceive an object as below, on the lower half as above, the horizon; and FIG.

primitives.name: Lateral Retinal Projection

primitives.assumptions: Lateral retinal stimulation inversely correlates with perceived horizontal object location.
primitives.breakdown_regime: At extreme lateral field-of-view or when retinal stimulation overlaps across hemispheres.

layer2.mapping: Encodes lateral displacement through inverse retinal coordinate transformation.
layer2.telemetry: Horizontal retinal offset and lateral object displacement

primitives.name: Neural Spread Function
primitives.verbatim_quote: The neural process is easily discovered, in the case of lateral extension or spreadoutness, to be the number of retinal nerve-ends affected by the light ; in the case of protension or mere farness it is more complicated and, as we have concluded, is still to seek.
primitives.assumptions: Neural spread scales linearly with retinal nerve-end activation count; distance perception is non-linear.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When neural activation exceeds threshold or when distance exceeds perceptual range.

layer2.mapping: Derives perceived object size and distance from retinal activation density.
layer2.telemetry: Retinal activation density and perceived object extent
